chunk_findings.detail: For a full-suite item run (`full=True`, `for_item=True`, `override=False`), `_plan` enters the `if for_item and not override:` branch and returns `scope = CS.plan(cfg, tree, base, requested="full")`. The function’s own contract in this diff says a full-suite run keeps “no planned scope”; the condition should also exclude `full` (`if for_item and not full and not override:`). As written, a full-suite item run gets an explicitly planned full scope instead of `None`, so callers can treat the full command as a planned/selected-scope run, contrary to the expected full-suite behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/runner.py:_plan

chunk_findings.detail: `lock_wait` is the suite-slot wait limit (it is passed directly as `wait_s` to `SL.hold`), while `budget` is the execution budget passed later to `_execute`. The line `budget = max(1, int(lock_wait) - int(waited))` therefore overwrites the command’s real budget with the remaining wait allowance. Concretely, if a run has a normal 600s command budget and a 30s per-run suite-wait override, and the slot is acquired almost immediately, `_execute` is called with `budget=30`, so a legitimate suite that would have been allowed 600s is killed at 30s.

chunk_findings.detail: The full-suite path still performs `with merge_tree(repo, sha, base, ...)` before `_run_under_slot`, and when that pre-slot merge yields `tree is None` it immediately returns a conflict/unavailable Result without ever waiting for or using the suite slot. For a full-suite run whose branch conflicts with the current base at enqueue while the suite slot is busy, the result is still decided by a merge tree built before the slot; if the base advances while the run would have queued, the post-wait merge could be clean, but this code has already failed the run. That violates the intended fix “merge after the slot is held” and preserves the pre-slot-merge race for the conflict case.

chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/runner.py: with merge_tree(...) / tree is None early return

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test only asserts that a `merge_enter` event appears somewhere after the first `hold_enter`. It never records or checks that `merge_enter` occurs before `hold_exit`. An implementation that enters the suite slot, immediately exits it, and only then merges would produce `events = ["hold_enter", "hold_exit", "merge_enter"]`; the test would pass even though no merge happened while the suite slot was held, which is exactly the invariant this change is supposed to enforce.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_merge_tree_after_queue_wait.py:test_the_fresh_merge_happens_inside_the_suite_slot

chunk_findings.detail: `_run_under_slot` uses `cfg` as a positional argument when calling `_execute`, but in `run` (around line 105 in the original code structure) `_execute` receives `cfg` as its first parameter; however, in `_run_under_slot` at line 192, `_execute` is called as `_execute(cfg, tree, cmd, scope, budget, tick, holding_suite=True, used=used)`. Inspecting `_execute`'s definition in `runner.py`, its signature is `_execute(repo, cfg, tree, cmd, scope, budget, tick, *, holding_suite=False, used=None)` (taking `repo` as the first argument, not `cfg`). Therefore, calling `_execute(cfg, tree, ...)` passes `Config` as the `repo` `Path` parameter, raising a `TypeError` or file-system error when `_execute` attempts to operate on `cfg` as a path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/runner.py:168

chunk_findings.detail: `lock_wait` is the suite-slot wait limit (`SL.hold(..., wait_s=lock_wait)`, and `_lock_wait` documents it as that), but once the slot is acquired the function throws away the execution `budget` and sets `budget = max(1, int(lock_wait) - int(waited))`. Given `budget=1800`, `lock_wait=60`, and a 59.1s queue wait, `_execute` is handed budget 1, so a suite that would pass is killed after one second and recorded as a CI failure. A short per-run wait override does the same even with no queue: `lock_wait=10`, `waited=0` caps a 30-minute suite at 10 seconds.

evidence.note: Claim: CI.run merges the branch with base before waiting for the host suite slot, so a base that moves during the wait leaves a stale tree. Refuted by: a full-suite run queued while base advances would test the old base and the baseline would read stale failures as new. Cheapest test: tests/test_ci_merge_tree_after_queue_wait.py::test_the_fresh_merge_happens_inside_the_suite_slot. Ran on unfixed head: FAILED (events=[merge_enter,hold_enter,hold_exit], no merge under the slot); on fixed head: PASSED. Cross-family reviewers gemini-3.5-flash-lite (google) and grok-4.7 (xai) confirmed the bug mechanism.

Rewrote CI.run: it now builds the merge tree when the checks run, not before the queue wait. A full-suite run merges afresh inside _run_under_slot (under the held slot); a named command merges once and takes no slot; a selected run merges once to plan its scope. Extracted _settle to keep runner.run under the complexity ratchet (run CC 19->21 grad D, now grade B). Regression test tests/test_ci_merge_tree_after_queue_wait.py fails on unfixed, passes on fixed. 98 related ci tests pass.
